issue.title: `onDownloadProgress` never emits `percent: 1` for empty response bodies

arms.better: TM found the right implementation quickly and recovered from its first no-progress attempt through an automatic retry. It should reduce repeated exploration and make the retry budget and continuation state clearer: the first attempt consumed 170,849 tokens before stopping at 10 steps, and its guidance said to resume the saved session while also saying a retry was scheduled. On the successful attempt, the transcript records running tests but does not make their result legible; the eventual code fix passes the Chromium hidden browser case, but independent hidden PR test files did not pass as a complete suite because Firefox/WebKit binaries were unavailable. Tool errors should also retain identifiers: `Tried to submit the ticket -> error: couldn't find that` gives no clue which resource was missing.

OpenCode stated a compact ordered plan, went directly to `source/utils/body.ts`, implemented the flush behavior, and added focused regression coverage. After the broad stream test timed out while exiting, it narrowed verification to the new stream test and ran XO and TypeScript checks, accurately noting the timeout in its final response. The independent PR browser regression then exposed a gap: Chromium emitted no progress event for the empty response in `test/browser.ts`, even though the added Node stream regression passed. It should reproduce and verify the real browser response path before finishing; the overall PR test files also remain blocked by unavailable Firefox/WebKit binaries and the pre-existing lint error.
